author: Robert Carr
description: Browned chicken, creamy white beans and kale in a rosemary broth finished with lemon, parsley and a little Parmesan. Three cans of beans give six substantial bowls body without heavy cream.
equipment: 8-quart Dutch oven or heavy soup pot with lid

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, unbrined, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tbsp (27 g) extra-virgin olive oil, divided into three 2-tsp portions
1 large yellow onion (250 g peeled), diced
3 medium carrots (250 g trimmed), cut into 1/4-inch dice
4 celery stalks (200 g trimmed), cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 tsp dried rosemary, crushed finely between your fingers
6 cups (1.44 L) low-sodium chicken broth, with 70 mg sodium or less per cup
3 cans (15 oz each) no-salt-added cannellini beans, drained and rinsed; about 720 g total, divided into 240 g mashed and 480 g whole beans
8 oz (227 g) kale leaves, tough stems removed, cut into bite-size pieces
1 oz (28 g) Parmesan cheese, finely grated
2 lemons, supplying 2 tsp finely grated zest and 1/4 cup (60 mL) juice
3/4 tsp (4.5 g) fine sea salt, divided into three 1/4-tsp portions
1/2 tsp black pepper, divided into two 1/4-tsp portions
instructions: Pat 1 1/2 lb (680 g) chicken breast pieces dry. Toss with 1/4 tsp (1.5 g) fine sea salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Mash 240 g drained cannellini beans with a fork; keep 480 g drained cannellini beans whole. Zest 2 lemons to obtain 2 tsp zest, then squeeze them to measure 1/4 cup (60 mL) juice.

Heat 2 tsp (9 g) olive oil in an 8-quart pot over medium-high heat. Add 340 g seasoned chicken in one layer. Brown for 3 minutes without moving, then turn and cook for 1 minute. Transfer to a bowl. Heat 2 tsp (9 g) olive oil in the pot and brown the second 340 g seasoned chicken for 3 minutes on the first side and 1 minute on the second. Transfer to the same bowl. The chicken is not fully cooked; continue the recipe immediately.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add 2 tsp (9 g) olive oil, 1 diced yellow onion (250 g), 3 diced carrots (250 g), 4 diced celery stalks (200 g), and 1/4 tsp (1.5 g) fine sea salt. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring and scraping, until softened with some golden edges. Keep the brown coating on the pot golden-brown, not black.

Stir in 2 tbsp (32 g) tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until brick-red. Add 6 minced garlic cloves (18 g), 2 tsp crushed dried rosemary, and 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Pour in 6 cups (1.44 L) low-sodium chicken broth and scrape up the browned coating. Stir in the 240 g mashed cannellini beans and 480 g whole cannellini beans. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cook partially covered for 8 minutes, until the carrots are nearly tender. Stir occasionally to prevent the mashed beans from sticking.

Add 8 oz (227 g) chopped kale and all browned chicken from the 680 g raw batch, including its collected juices. Simmer gently for 5-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the kale is tender and several of the largest chicken pieces reach 165 F (74 C). Use the temperature rather than the clock, and stop simmering once the chicken is done.

Turn off the heat. Stir in 1 oz (28 g) finely grated Parmesan, 2 tsp lemon zest, 1/4 cup (60 mL) lemon juice, 1/2 cup (20 g) chopped parsley, 1/4 tsp (1.5 g) fine sea salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Rest for 5 minutes, then stir well and divide the complete batch evenly among 6 servings, distributing chicken and beans evenly. The finished broth should be creamy but spoonable, savory and distinctly lemony, not dominated by salt.
notes: Flavor: brown the chicken in two uncrowded batches, crush the rosemary, and cook the tomato paste before adding broth. Mashed beans provide body; the measured Parmesan adds depth without making this a cream soup. Add the lemon after cooking so it stays bright.

Health-conscious design: unbrined lean chicken, three cans of no-salt-added beans, substantial vegetables, measured olive oil and a small amount of cheese. Broth and Parmesan still contribute sodium; low-sodium and unsalted labels are not interchangeable, so check the sodium per cup. This is an editorial recipe choice, not a medical or low-sodium certification.

Can yields vary. Use the contents of all three drained cans; mash one can and keep two cans whole. The 240 g / 480 g split is the expected drained yield, not a reason to discard beans or buy another can for a small weight difference.

Meal prep: stir and divide into 6 shallow containers rather than cooling the entire pot on the counter. Refrigerate at 40 F (4 C) or below within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when the room is above 90 F (32 C). Use refrigerated portions within 3-4 days. Freeze portions for later days on prep day; allow expansion room and use within 3 months for best planned quality. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, not on the counter.

Reheat one portion with 2 tbsp (30 mL) water in a saucepan, stirring frequently. Bring the soup briefly to a rolling boil and verify the chicken and center of the portion reach 165 F (74 C); do not keep boiling after that. For microwave reheating, cover loosely, stir halfway and check several spots reach 165 F (74 C). Reheat only the portion being eaten.

Allergens: milk from Parmesan; check broth labels for any additional allergens. Six equal portions are the serving definition; the finished cup volume depends on evaporation. Optional bread or other sides are not part of the base recipe.
Developed and reviewed in writing; not yet kitchen-tested. Numerical nutrition estimates are not published because final product labels and a complete calculation have not been verified.
